Good morning. Teresa Nunes. Last Tuesday, at eleven at night, we were finalizing the contract. I was reading the last version, Marina was checking the numbers, and the broker was waiting on the telephone in London. At a quarter past eleven the buyer sent a counter-offer, and that interrupted everything. While I was reading it, Marina found the mistake: the price was right, but the date was wrong. We called the broker at midnight. He confirmed the new date, and we signed at ten past twelve.

Eduardo, Paulo here. I want to tell you what happened in the Cairo deal, because we were doing everything right. In October we were finishing due diligence, and the two sides were already agreeing on the price. While the lawyers were writing the last version, the regulator asked for one more document. Nobody sent it. I was waiting for the bank, and the bank was waiting for us. Six weeks later the buyer backed out. The document was two pages. It was on my desk.
